book.title: Journey to the East: The Jesuit Mission to China, 1579-1724

evidence: academic press signal: Belknap Press / Harvard University Press
academic press signal: Belknap Press / Harvard University Press

argument.statement: Jesuit missionaries translated Roman Catholicism into the Chinese cultural frame, making sustained engagement with Chinese language and thought central to their conversion effort.

book.rationale: The book focuses on the Jesuit Mission to China within a global historical context, prominently exploring the interactions between cultures during a specific historical period.
book.summary: It was one of the great encounters of world history: highly educated European priests confronting Chinese culture for the first time in the modern era. This “journey to the East” is explored by Liam Brockey as he retraces the path of the Jesuit missionaries who sailed from Portugal to China, believing that, with little more than firm conviction and divine assistance, they could convert the Chinese to Christianity. Moving beyond the image of Jesuits as cultural emissaries, his book shows how these priests, in the first concerted European effort to engage with Chinese language and thought, translated Roman Catholicism into the Chinese cultural frame and eventually claimed two hundred thousand converts. The first narrative history of the Jesuits’ mission from 1579 until the proscription of Christianity in China in 1724, this study is also the first to use extensive documentation of the enterprise found in Lisbon and Rome. The peril of travel in the premodern world, the danger of entering a foreign land alone and unarmed, and the challenge of understanding a radically different culture result in episodes of high drama set against such backdrops as the imperial court of Peking, the villages of Shanxi Province, and the bustling cities of the Yangzi Delta region.
